page: Amazon Web Services c7i.large is an entry-level compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is provisioned with 2 vCPUs derived from a single dedicated physical core of an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at a base clock of 3.2 GHz. The instance configuration features 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio. The processor architecture includes support for instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives.

The instance does not include bundled local instance storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage solutions, and contains no discrete graphics hardware. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps. In terms of compute and throughput benchmarks, single-threaded execution performs within median industry percentiles, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1665.0 and a single-core stress-ng result of 1938.18. Conversely, due to its low overall core count, multi-threaded metrics rank lower across tests, including a multi-core Geekbench score of 2034.0, a PassMark CPU score of 3589.52, and a static web serving throughput of 3.93 GB/sec.

Hardware-level memory throughput is limited on this smaller allocation, registering 11.05 GB/sec on large read blocks and 11.76 GB/sec on large write blocks. Redis throughput reaches 2.35 million operations per second, while small-model LLM inference achieves 287.25 tokens per second for prompt processing and 54.88 tokens per second for generation. Given the single physical core allocation and compact memory footprint, the c7i.large offers an entry-tier x86 option for workloads that benefit from modern Intel instructions but require minimal concurrency, such as lightweight web serving, dedicated microservices, batch processing, and CI/CD agent runners.

The CPU includes instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AMX. The instance includes no local storage or GPUs, providing a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate average single-threaded performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1665.0 and stress-ng score of 1938.18, alongside single-threaded compression throughput reaching 28.29 GB/sec. Due to its dual-thread single-core capacity, aggregate throughput metrics rank lower, including a PassMark CPU score of 3589.52 and web serving throughput of 3.93 GB/sec. This configuration functions efficiently for lightweight microservices, small CI/CD build agents, and basic web serving.
